title: One core — what needs your call before merging

steps.intro: Review found no security hole and no lost feature. These are the gaps worth closing first.

steps.path: Any chat, opened on a phone connected to your computer
steps.headline: When the phone and computer are on different app versions, should the screen say which one to update?
steps.today: The phone and the computer now speak a new shared language. The PR says both should be updated together, but nothing makes that happen — the computer updates itself, the Android app doesn't.
steps.problem: New phone + old computer: chats look empty with a 'may be out of date' strip, and Refresh fails the same way. Old Android app + new computer: every chat shows one line, 'Refresh this page to finish updating' — wrong advice, an app has no page to refresh. Either way it looks like lost chats.
steps.proposal: Show one clear sentence naming the device that needs updating. Both sides already send a version number; nothing reads it yet. Small job.

options.label: Add the message
pros: The first person on mismatched versions knows exactly what to do.
Avoids 'my chats are gone' reports that are really just an update.
cons: A little more work before merging.

options.label: Merge without it
cons: Anyone not updated on both devices sees empty or stuck chats with no explanation.

steps.path: Every feature a paired phone can use on your computer
steps.headline: Should new features be closed to phones unless someone marks them phone-safe?
steps.today: When a feature is added, a phone can use it automatically unless the builder remembers to mark it 'computer only'. An automatic test catches a forgotten label, but only when the tests run.
steps.problem: One forgotten label could quietly let a paired phone do something on your computer it shouldn't. The old setup was the opposite: closed unless allowed.
steps.proposal: Flip it: phones get a feature only when it is marked phone-safe. You'd notice nothing; it's a few dozen one-word labels in the code.

options.label: Closed unless allowed
pros: A mistake hides a feature from the phone instead of exposing it.
Matches how it worked before this PR.
cons: A new phone feature is missing on the phone until someone labels it.

options.label: Keep it open by default
pros: No extra work; the test still catches mistakes.
cons: Safety depends on a test running, not on the design.

steps.path: Reading project instruction files from a phone
steps.headline: Should the 'never show a phone this file' check always run when a phone reads instruction files?
steps.today: A phone can now read your project instruction files. Before handing one over, the computer checks a blocklist of private files (passwords, keys).
steps.problem: That check is skipped if the answer comes back without a file location attached. I couldn't confirm that ever happens, but if it does, a blocked file could reach the phone.
steps.proposal: Yes: make the check run every time — a one-line change, nothing you'd notice. No: leave it as is.

steps.intro: You okayed these on Sept 30 and Oct 1. Now that they're built, confirm they should stay. Anyone holding a paired phone gets them.

steps.path: Things a paired phone can now do on your computer
steps.headline: Which of these new phone powers should stay allowed? Unpicked ones become computer-only.
steps.today: A paired phone can now do all four of these on your computer. Before this PR it could do none of them.
steps.problem: Each one acts as you. If a paired phone is lost or someone else uses it, they could do these too.
steps.proposal: Pick the ones to keep on the phone. Anything left unpicked becomes computer-only; nothing else changes.

options.label: Install and remove themes
pros: Change your look from the couch.
cons: Someone holding your phone could change your theme (appearance only).

options.label: Publish themes
pros: Share a theme without going to the computer.
cons: Opens a public GitHub pull request under your account.

options.label: Rate, comment and report
pros: Use the marketplace fully from the phone.

options.label: Update plugins
cons: Changes what runs on your computer.

steps.page: Things to watch, and small tidy-ups
steps.intro: Lower stakes. Quick yes or no.

steps.path: Running several Claude Code chats at once
steps.headline: Is it okay to merge and just watch for slowdown with several chats running at once?
steps.today: To spot pop-ups like 'Switch model?', the computer now keeps a hidden screen reader for every Claude Code chat, even ones you're not looking at.
steps.problem: With three or more chats streaming at the same time, typing might feel a bit slower. Not measured — it may be fine.

options.label: Merge, watch for it
pros: No delay; you check it during your real-device test.
If it's slow, it gets fixed then.
cons: If it is slow, you'll feel it before the fix.

options.label: Measure first
cons: Delays the merge for something that may be fine.

steps.path: Pop-ups like 'Switch model?' inside a chat
steps.headline: Is a tenth-of-a-second delay in spotting pop-ups acceptable?
steps.today: When Claude Code shows a pop-up, the app blocks your typing box so you don't type into it by mistake.
steps.problem: That block can now arrive up to a tenth of a second late. Typing and pressing Enter in that instant could send your message into the pop-up. The PR admits this.
steps.proposal: Yes: accept it, it's rare. No: I'll look for a way to close the gap before merging.

steps.path: Notes and checks assistants read; nothing in the app
steps.headline: Should I do the bundle of small tidy-ups on both PRs?
steps.today: Several notes are out of date after this work.
steps.problem: About ten to-do items still say work is 'planned' that this PR finishes. Three phone-test items overlap. The start-here page contradicts itself. One rules note every session loads is double its size limit. A comment names a test that doesn't exist. Also a dev-tool bug: a crashed test copy could make a later launch stop an unrelated program on your computer (never your real app).
steps.proposal: Yes: fix all of these and push to the same PRs. Nothing in the app changes. No: leave them for after the merge.

steps.headline: Merge the app PR first, then re-run the workspace PR's checks before merging it.
steps.changed: The workspace PR's automatic checks are red right now only because they look for app files that don't exist until the app PR merges.
steps.notice: After the app merges, those checks should turn green. If they don't, something is really wrong and I'll tell you.
